items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: my wife went to the Lieutenant, to speak to him on my behalf. His name was Lieutenant Danzinger.

ctx.x: So you were able to do that instead of get shipped overseas?

That’s right. We were all sent overseas just the day before I was transferred. In other words, after I was transferred to the Army Air Force Band at Ft. Dix, they went right © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

overseas. We were at the Port of Embarkation, Monk, at Camp Kilmer, New Jersey. I’ll never forget that. And we knew we were going to go overseas in a matter of a day or two. And my wife went to the Lieutenant, to speak to him on my behalf. His name was Lieutenant Danzinger. Look how I remember that name, 50 years ago. D-A-N-Z-I-N-G- E-R. Lieutenant Danzinger.
